items.stem: Why should a Power Automate-triggered Office Script avoid Workbook.getActiveWorksheet?

options.text: Automated runs have no reliable active selection, so named references are safer
options.rationale: Correct: flows should reference objects by consistent names, not relative/active state.

options.text: getActiveWorksheet is not a valid API
options.rationale: It is valid; it is just unreliable in automation.
It is an Office Scripts API, not VBA.

items.explanation: Correct: flows should reference objects by consistent names, not relative/active state.

items.stem: Which TWO are recommended defensive practices in Office Scripts? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Check that a worksheet or table exists before calling methods on it
options.rationale: Correct: guarding against missing objects prevents abrupt failures.

options.text: Use the Action Recorder to learn how an API is called
options.rationale: Correct: recording is the easiest way to discover the correct API calls.

options.text: Assume every workbook always contains the expected sheet
options.rationale: Sheets can be renamed or removed between runs.

options.text: Hard-code cell colours so the script cannot be reused
options.rationale: Parameterising improves reuse; hard-coding reduces it.

items.explanation: Correct: guarding against missing objects prevents abrupt failures.

items.stem: Office Scripts are written primarily in which language?

options.rationale: Correct: Office Scripts use TypeScript (a superset of JavaScript).
